summary: **Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions** is a software system designed to continuously monitor astronauts' health during space missions. It tracks vital signs such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, and body temperature. The system helps detect health problems early, stores medical data, and supports timely medical decisions, ensuring astronauts' safety and well-being.
details:
Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions (SpaceCare)

SpaceCare is a health monitoring software designed to monitor and manage the health information of astronauts during space missions. The application provides a centralized platform to record, store, access, and manage astronauts' health records. It allows astronauts to view their health-related information, while administrators can securely log in to manage astronaut details and monitor health records. The system uses a database to store health information and provides an organized, user-friendly interface for efficient data management.

The main benefit of this project is to improve astronaut healthcare and safety during space missions. It reduces manual record-keeping, provides quick access to health information, improves data organization, and supports better medical decision-making. The intended impact is to contribute to safer and more efficient healthcare management, especially during long-duration space missions where immediate medical assistance may not be available.

The project was developed using Python as the primary programming language, FastAPI as the backend framework, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for frontend development, and SQLite for database management. Visual Studio Code was used as the development environment, and a web browser was used for testing the application. A computer or laptop was used as the development hardware.

The creative aspect of SpaceCare is its application of modern web technologies to the specialized field of astronaut healthcare. It combines administrator authentication, health record management, and an interactive web interface into a single platform. While developing the project, our team considered important factors such as user-friendly design, data security, accuracy, reliability, accessibility, and future scalability. We also considered the possibility of integrating wearable health sensors and real-time health monitoring devices in future versions. Overall, SpaceCare aims to provide a foundation for smarter healthcare management in space exploration and contribute to the health and safety of astronauts.
